class.name: TimeOfDay
class.brief_description: Moves a sun and a moon across the sky as the hours pass, and dims the sky at night.
class.description: Add a [TimeOfDay] with two [DirectionalLight3D] children: the first is the sun and the second the moon (or set [member sun] and [member moon]). As [member time] passes, it points them from where they are in the sky, sets their energy and color (warm and low at dawn and dusk, white at noon, a dim blue moon at night) and turns off whichever is below the horizon. In a running game it also dims the sky, the ambient light and the fog's light of the world's [Environment] at night, down to [member night_sky_energy] of their own values. The moon goes through its phases as the days pass ([member moon_phase]): a full moon rises as the sun sets and lights the night, a new one is beside the sun and gives no light. The stars turn round the celestial pole with the hours. The skies ([CloudySkyMaterial], [AtmosphereSkyMaterial]) draw both. Everything in the [code]night_lights[/code] group (street lamps, lit windows, a sign) is shown once it's dark and hidden again in daylight, each at a slightly different moment, the same one every time, so a street's lamps come on one by one. Under heavy cloud they come on sooner. The sun rises in the node's +X direction and is due +Z at noon, so turn the node to set where north is. In the editor, changing [member time] shows that hour, but the clock only runs in a game. For shaders, it sets the shader globals [code]time_of_day_sun_direction[/code], [code]time_of_day_moon_direction[/code], [code]time_of_day_star_rotation[/code] and [code]time_of_day_night[/code] ([code]0[/code] in daylight to [code]1[/code] at night, for windows that glow at night).

method.name: get_daylight
method.description: How much daylight there is: [code]1.0[/code] by day, [code]0.0[/code] at night, and in between round sunrise and sunset.

method.name: get_moon_direction
method.description: Towards the moon, in global space: as far behind the sun as its phase, so a full moon is opposite the sun.

method.name: get_moon_light
method.description: How much of the moon's face is lit, from [code]0[/code] (new) to [code]1[/code] (full). The moon's light is this much of [member moon_energy].

method.name: get_star_rotation
method.description: The rotation from the stars' own directions to where they are in the sky now, turning round the celestial pole with the hours.

method.name: get_sun_direction
method.description: The direction towards the sun, in global space.

method.name: is_day
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while the sun is above the horizon.

members.member: How many real seconds a day takes. [code]0[/code] stops the clock.
How far north (or south, below [code]0[/code]) the place is, in degrees: the further from the equator, the lower the sun stays.
The light for the moon. When it's empty, the first [DirectionalLight3D] child that isn't the sun is used.
The moon's energy when it's high in the sky.
Where the moon is in its phases, from [code]0[/code] (new) through [code]0.5[/code] (full) back to [code]1[/code]. It moves on as the clock runs, a whole cycle every 29.5 days.
How bright the sky and ambient light are at night, as a part of their own energies.
How much cloud covers the sky, from [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code]: at [code]1[/code], a fifth of the sun's and moon's light gets through. A [Weather3D] beside it sets this as the weather changes.
The light for the sun. When it's empty, the first [DirectionalLight3D] child is used.
The sun's energy when it's high in the sky.
The time of day in hours, from [code]0.0[/code] (midnight) to [code]24.0[/code]: [code]13.5[/code] is half past one in the afternoon.

signal.name: hour_changed
signal.description: Emitted as each hour begins, with the hour from [code]0[/code] to [code]23[/code]: for every hour in turn, even when a frame spans several.
